chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is leading the people in prayer, then breaks his state of purity, and puts forward a man who has missed one rakʿah. What should he do? He said: He should not put forward one who has missed one rakʿah; rather, he should take the hand of someone else and put him forward.

So this report, even though its apparent wording is the apparent wording of prohibition, we interpret it as indicating a type of dislikeability, based on the indication of the reports that came earlier.

key_terms.سُبِقَ بِرَكْعَةٍ: has missed one rakʿah behind the congregation
key_terms.فَيُحْدِثُ: enters a state that nullifies ritual purity during prayer
key_terms.لَا يُقَدِّمُ: he should not appoint or put forward
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads the people in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.ٱلْأَخْبَارِ: the narrations or hadith reports used as evidence
key_terms.ٱلْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikeability rather than strict prohibition in this context

ai.seo_question: Can an Imam who breaks wudu (ablution) during congregational prayer appoint someone who missed a rakʿah to lead?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling for congregational salat (prayer) when the Imam loses ritual purity during the prayer and needs to appoint someone else to complete it. The report states that he should not appoint someone who has missed a rakʿah, though the compiler explains that this is understood as karāhah rather than strict prohibition in light of other narrations.
